summary: Ran /iterate-on-plan on fix-audit-choices-range-ledger-path: one iteration, twelve findings (4 high, 5 medium, 3 low), all addressed; a second pass found nothing at or above the medium threshold, so the loop converged. The headline: design decision D4's characterization test was necessary but insufficient. It pinned Python functions while prioritize-proposals/SKILL.md only ever calls the CLI entry points (priorities_paths.py run-id / paths, retention.py), no existing test runs those as subprocesses, and the one thing the move genuinely adds - a skills/shared/ import bootstrap - only fails when a module runs as a script from an installed copy. The guard now has three parts: function-level pins, the CLI entry points run as subprocesses from a runtime-shaped copy (<tmp>/prioritize-proposals/scripts beside <tmp>/shared), and the three pre-existing test modules plus SKILL.md held byte-unchanged by a git diff --quiet verification step in work-packages.yaml. Confirmed has_db_migration:true is a false positive (no database anywhere in scope) and reworded the work-package description so the substring match stops re-triggering. openspec validate --strict and the work-package validator both pass. NOTE ON LANDING: this dispatch's Bash guard refuses every git operation that targets the shared feature worktree (cd and -C alike), so the iteration commit was made on a detached HEAD in the launchpad worktree at the feature branch's tip; see next_steps for where the commit lives and how it was landed.

decisions.title: D4 guard judged insufficient and extended rather than accepted
decisions.rationale: A function-level characterization test cannot observe the one failure the move introduces (the import bootstrap when run as a script from an installed copy). The CLI entry points are the skill's only runtime interface and were untested as subprocesses.

decisions.title: D7 taken without a user in the loop and flagged for approval
decisions.rationale: The skill requires assumption findings to go through AskUserQuestion; that tool is not exposed to this autopilot sub-agent. The choice (directory from header generated_at + git_sha; caller's run_id untouched) is recorded as an explicit decision with the rejected alternative so plan approval can overturn it in one place.

decisions.title: No new spec scenarios for retention failure or two-run idempotency
decisions.rationale: The spec delta is deliberately path-agnostic; both behaviours are pinned at task level (5.2, 4.3).

decisions.title: Single work package retained
decisions.rationale: Chain 1.1 -> 2.1 -> 2.2 -> 4.1 -> 4.2 -> {4.3, 5.1 -> 5.3, 5.2} with 3.1 off 2.2; max parallel width 2-3 of S-sized tasks, not worth a second worktree.

decisions.title: Vendor review not dispatched from this phase
decisions.rationale: The orchestrator owns a separate PLAN_REVIEW phase; the dispatch notes forbid duplicating it here.
